                                              PUC PROJECT NO. 59142


                                                         §
              REVIEW OF ERCOT'S                          §
                                                         §     PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
    INTERCONNECTION PROCESSES FOR                        §
                                                         §                 OF TEXAS
                  LARGE LOADS                            §



                                             I.​     INTRODUCTION


        Schaper Energy Consulting LLC (“Respondent”) advises hyperscale data center developers who

have invested significant capital in reliance on the stable framework promised by PGRR115 and Section 9

of the ERCOT Planning Guide. We file these comments to address ERCOT’s verbal comments to the

Commission on December 18, 2025, which effectively signal an abandonment of the PGRR115 Large

Load Interconnection Study (LLIS) process, a protocol implemented only 72 hours prior. This sudden

pivot to an undefined ‘batch study’ procedure threatens to undermine transparency and discard

stakeholder-approved protocols. In addition to penalizing compliant participants, it could erase years of

development progress. ERCOT’s unannounced reversal introduces severe regulatory risk and undermines

the certainty essential for continued investment. An abrupt regulatory change without sufficient

transparency or thorough stakeholder engagement is not aligned with the stable regulatory environment

for which Texas has historically been recognized and risks eroding confidence in ERCOT.


                                      II.​         CURRENT SITUATION


​       ERCOT leadership used the December 18, 2025, meeting to compare the large load

interconnection queue to a popular “restaurant” that has become congested because it lacks a “reservation

system” that entails customer commitment.1 However, ERCOT’s solution, abandoning the current

framework for a ‘batch study’ process, defies the logic of their own metaphor. It is akin to a manager

        1
            ERCOT CEO Pablo Vegas, Remarks at PUC open meeting December 18, 2025
 handling a dinner rush by forcing eager patrons into the parking lot to wait for whatever the kitchen cooks

up.


​        The Commission must rigorously evaluate the objectives behind ERCOT’s proposed procedural

changes. Proposals that merely reduce planning workloads or offer theoretical electrical engineering

solutions, without resulting in projects that can be capitalized and constructed, will not be viewed as

viable by the market. Consistent with Senate Bill 6, the Commission must ensure any new approach

serves all stakeholders by reliably energizing large loads and promoting business development while

minimizing stranded costs.


                     III.​   PROCEDURAL AND SUBSTANTIVE OBJECTIONS


         Respondent objects to the impromptu introduction of the ‘batch study’ methodology and

respectfully requests that the Commission deny any future ERCOT request for a ‘good cause’ exception

related to this matter. Instead, the Commission should direct ERCOT to continue processing large load

interconnection requests pursuant to the established Planning Guide Section 9 rules currently in effect

until its rulemaking on this topic concludes and those rules are adopted.


         A strategic pivot of this magnitude, attempted by fiat rather than through established stakeholder

processes, cannot be justified. ERCOT’s proposal, as introduced publicly for the first time on December

18, 2025, lacks procedural transparency, disrupts logical sequencing, and preempts Commission

rulemaking; it relies on ill-advised exceptions to protocol and risks economic harm to market participants.

Our objection is detailed further below based on four principles.


      1.​ Procedural Opacity and Failure of Notice: ERCOT’s development of the ‘batch study’ plan

         was devoid of detail and introduced without prior notice or documentation at the Commission’s

         final open meeting of 2025. This irregularity deprived stakeholders of a meaningful opportunity

         to comment. Commissioners immediately noted the discrepancy, questioning why the filed
    documents related to PGRR115 implementation bore no relation to ERCOT’s verbal presentation

   and lacked supporting materials2. By bypassing the Large Load Working Group, the Technical

   Advisory Committee, and other established stakeholder forums, ERCOT circumvented the

   stakeholder process and limited public notice on this matter. Furthermore, after submitting

   detailed implementation Q&A related to PGRR115 in advance of the PUC open meeting, ERCOT

   effectively signaled a partial abandonment of the relevant Planning Guide section just 72 hours

   later, omitting the topic from their presentation almost entirely.


2.​ Inappropriate Sequencing and Preemption of Commission Rulemaking: We believe

   ERCOT’s introduction of the 'batch study' concept is premature, as it preempts active

   Commission rulemaking that will directly and positively impact this process. By unilaterally

   interjecting an undefined ‘batch study,’ ERCOT subverts the collaborative development of

   Uniform Financial Commitment rules under PURA §37.0561, which stakeholders are specifically

   designing to address the queue management challenges that ERCOT cites as the rationale for this

   new process. We request that the Commission direct ERCOT to continue processing projects that

   meet imminent financial readiness criteria and defer consideration of structural overrides to

   Planning Guide Section 9 until the Commission's rulemakings directed at the large load process

   take effect. Discarding diligent stakeholder efforts on these rulemakings by fiat sends a damaging

   signal that market participant input is not valued and efforts to adhere to those rules would be

   proven meaningless.


3.​ Defective Reliance on ‘Good Cause’ Exception: ERCOT indicated a willingness to pursue a

   ‘good cause’ exception to seek relief under the recently enacted PGRR115 provisions in Planning

   Guide Section 93. Relying on a ‘good cause’ exception to implement an untested, novel study

   process without formal socialization with stakeholders is legally dubious and evades necessary


   2
       Commissioner Hjaltman, Remarks at PUC open meeting December 18, 2025
   3
       ERCOT SVP Chad Seely, Remarks at PUC open meeting December 18, 2025
         scrutiny. A change of this magnitude requires transparent input consistent with established

        protocol. Fundamentally, ERCOT is seeking emergency powers to address a backlog it has

        actively worsened through its own actions, the result of a long-standing failure to adequately

        resource large-load interconnection study review or to adhere to interim guidelines. Because this

        administrative challenge was foreseeable and self-inflicted, it fails to meet the legal standard for

        ‘good cause’.


    4.​ Economic Harm and Market Uncertainty: Texas is positioned to capture over $500 billion in

        digital infrastructure investment, but realizing this opportunity requires regulatory stability.

        ERCOT’s recent ‘batch study’ proposal introduced unnecessary uncertainty into the market

        because it lacked timelines, criteria, and supporting documentation – despite adequate time to

        provide such information. Unilateral protocol changes and ambiguous directives risk driving

        capital toward more predictable jurisdictions. We strongly urge ERCOT leadership to adopt a

        communication strategy prioritizing transparency to safeguard the significant investments

        currently underway and restore market confidence.


                                  III.​   PROPOSED RESOLUTION


        We respectfully propose that the Commission adopt a sequential approach to ERCOT’s proposal

regarding study procedure modifications to Planning Guide Section 9. First, the Commission should

defer any action on ERCOT’s plan to shift to a ‘batch study’ methodology. Instead, priority must be

placed on expeditiously finalizing and implementing the rulemakings related to the Rulemaking to

Implement Large Load Interconnection Standards Under PURA §37.0561, which introduces, among other

things, uniform financial commitments into the large load interconnection process. Only after these

financial measures are in force, and their ability to filter the interconnection queue has been observed,

should the Commission entertain alterations to the current serial study methodology.
         The necessity of this sequence stems from our assessment that the current backlog of large load

planning studies is driven primarily by a lack of financial friction, rather than a failure of the serial study

process itself. The absence of uniform financial commitments has inflated the queue, directly contributing

to the delays that led ERCOT to postpone PGRR115 implementation and now propose its partial

abandonment. We believe the Commission may underestimate the extent to which this lack of uniform

financial commitment encourages speculative entries, thereby overwhelming ERCOT’s planning

resources.


        As active participants in this process, we have witnessed the practical consequences of this

regulatory gap. We have observed instances in which utilities failed to collect both study fees and security

before ERCOT resources were allocated, and in which studies were approved before developers could

comment on the findings. In some cases, these approvals were granted despite the developer having risked

no capital. This dynamic misallocates critical ERCOT resources to projects with uncertain capacity and

questionable or nonexistent developer commitment.


        The serial study process remains a viable framework when paired with sufficient uniform

financial commitment. Therefore, we urge the Commission to implement the financial measures

mandated by Senate Bill 6 as soon as possible. These safeguards are essential regardless of the study

methodology used, and their implementation may reveal that abandoning the current Planning Guide

Section 9 elements is unnecessary.


                                           IV.​   CONCLUSION


        We urge the Commission to consider the impact of this proposal on market confidence carefully.

Encouraging ERCOT to propose unilateral action with only token stakeholder engagement creates

uncertainty and runs counter to the goal of Senate Bill 6 to support business development. We ask the

Commission to direct ERCOT to utilize established stakeholder channels moving forward, ensuring the

stability and due process necessary to protect investment in the state.
